questions.question: What is the worst-case time for a lookup in a hash table, and when does it happen?
options: O(log n), when the table is resizing
O(n), when many keys collide into the same bucket
O(n²), when the load factor is below 0.75
questions.explanation: Lookups are O(1) on average. If all keys land in one bucket, the lookup has to scan a list of n entries, which is O(n).

questions.question: What does `const m = new Map([[[1, 2], "x"]]); m.get([1, 2])` return?
options: undefined, because array keys are compared by reference
questions.explanation: Map compares object keys by reference. The second [1, 2] is a different array, so there is no match. Use a string key like "1,2" instead.

questions.question: In the hash-map Two Sum solution, why do we check for the complement before inserting the current number?
options: It is faster to check first
Map.set fails if the key already exists
So an element is never paired with itself, e.g. target 600 with a single 300
questions.explanation: If we inserted first, a lone 300 would find itself as the complement of 600. Checking first means the map only contains earlier indices.

questions.question: Why is the Set-based longest consecutive sequence solution O(n) despite having a while loop inside a for loop?
options: Because the inner loop only starts at numbers whose predecessor is missing, so each number is walked over at most once in total
Because the input is sorted first
questions.explanation: Skipping any x where x - 1 exists means each run is counted once from its start. Across all runs, the inner loop does O(n) total work.
